## Parity

> [!thm] Theorem 1
> The sum of two even numbers is even.
^even-sum

> [!proof]- Proof (d 1)
> 1. Write the two numbers as $2a$ and $2b$.
> 2. Their sum is $2(a + b)$, which is even.

> [!derive] Show that the square of an odd number is odd.
^d-odd-square

> [!solution]- Solution
> 1. Write the odd number as $2k + 1$.
> 2. Its square is $4k^2 + 4k + 1 = 2(2k^2 + 2k) + 1$, which is odd.

> [!derive] Show that the cube of an even number is a multiple of 8.
^d-even-cube

> [!solution]- Solution
> 1. Write the even number as $2k$; its cube is $8k^3$.

> [!problem] Consecutive product (d 2)
> Show that $n^2 + n$ is even for every integer $n$.
^inv-fx-consecutive

> [!solution]- Solution
> methods: parity
> 1. $n^2 + n = n(n + 1)$, and one of two consecutive integers is even.
